reason: Conversation 1 gives a fuller, safer diagnosis: it links the crushed hose to the very hot cabinet and the cut-out tripping, advises unplugging and letting it cool, suggests a cheap replacement hose if it won't spring back, and gives a clear test and escalation path if it persists. It also answers the landlord question properly, covering written notice, agreeing the hose cost first, and that a persistent fault is the landlord's engineer's job. Conversation 2 is correct on the fix but terse and repetitive, with garbled template text ('and condenser on condensers'). It never addresses the landlord's responsibility, offers no escalation, and gives only minimal safety guidance beyond the panel text. Conversation 1 is slightly wordy and has formatting glitches, but it is far more useful and complete.
